driver.text: Tech sold off on renewed AI-spending-return worries after Tesla and Meta earnings (Meta -8%, its largest drop since July; Lam Research -10% despite record results). items.headline: China market regulator urges 9 e-commerce platforms to tighten quality controls; Alibaba's Hong Kong shares close down 6.2%
items.summary: SAMR's Oct 21 notice (counterfeits, mismatched descriptions, false advertising) hit Alibaba's HK shares, which closed at HK$97.30 (-6.17%), the steepest drop in about two months. The US ADR closed Oct 21 at $104.41 (-3.87%) and traded near $99.60 premarket Oct 22; its Oct 22 close was not verified. Regulatory scrutiny can raise compliance costs and pressure the multiple.

items.headline: Alibaba leads Hong Kong tech slide on China regulatory move
items.summary: Hang Seng fell as much as 3% and Hang Seng Tech as much as 4.7%. Analysts also pointed to the end of a 90-day grace period for offshore trust taxes, linked to recent stake sales by major shareholders.

items.headline: Nvidia falls over 4% as chip stocks slide on AI financing worries
items.summary: SOX down over 6% intraday. Concerns include the cost of funding AI buildouts, circular-financing worries (reported ~$2.8B Nvidia/Tesla investment in Samsung Electro-Mechanics) and higher oil. Jensen Huang said neocloud demand is very strong but capital availability is the constraint.

items.headline: Steep bill for AI buildout punishes Meta and other tech favourites
items.summary: Meta -8% on negative free cash flow and a new non-voting share class; Lam Research -10% as supply constraints limited guidance; neocloud names CoreWeave and Nebius fell. Questions on AI ROI weigh on Nvidia's demand outlook.
